newsitem.title: USA: CME HOGS AND PORK BELLIES SEEN STEADY TO LOWER.
newsitem.headline: CME HOGS AND PORK BELLIES SEEN STEADY TO LOWER.

text.p: CME lean hog futures were expected to open steady to 0.150 cent per lb lower while pork belly futures were called steady to 0.250 cent lower, livestock analysts said.
Steady to lower cash hog indications again Wednesday and expectations cash markets could stay under pressure the rest of the week were expected to weigh on hog futures.
Also, wholesale pork has been showing less-than-expected demand and pork cutout values slipped again on Tuesday which will keep packer bids for cash hogs down, analysts said.
Latest CME lean hog index was off $0.19 at $79.23 per cwt.

Pork belly futures were expected to come under early pressure as cash bellies continued weak. Expectations had been for product prices to bottom but a recent increase in fresh belly production has kept pressure on cash prices and Tuesday's out-of-town report was only neutral, they said.
The CME reported a net out-movement of 3.516 million lbs from warehouses outside Chicago, well within the range of trade estimates of out 3.0 millin to 3.7 million lbs.
However, August could again show support as deliveries appear to be in strong hands, they added.
